newsitem.title: USA: AMC Entertainment to sell $200 mln in junk bonds.
newsitem.headline: AMC Entertainment to sell $200 mln in junk bonds.

text.p: AMC Entertainment Inc one the largest U.S. movie theater companies, is expected to sell $200 million in junk bonds over the next several weeks, high-yield players said.
Market sources say the offering, which will be jointly underwritten by Goldman Sachs & Co and Salomon Brothers Inc, will consist of $200 million in senior subordinated notes due 2009.
Proceeds from the offering will be used to refinance bank debt, they said.
A company spokewoman as well as Craig Ramsey, vice president of finance at AMC, declined to comment.

The offering will not be the first time AMC has tapped the junk-bond market. AMC issued $100 million in senior notes and $100 million in senior subordinated in 1992. The company redeemed both issues in 1995, partly with borrowings from a revolving credit facility.
Alan Ginsberg, head of high-yield research at Smith Barney Inc, noted the movie theater industry is not unfamiliar to high-yield investors.
"It's not been the largest sector of the high-yield bond market, but it has been a consistent performer," he said.

He said movie theater companies are likely to experience steady growth in the future, particularly internationally. He noted the movie theater business is known for its stablity and resistance to macro-economic cycles.

"Basically, going to the movies is an enormously popular form of entertainment in the U.S. and around the world. Economically, it continues to be a bargain versus other forms of entertainment out of the home such as concerts of sporting events.
AMC is currently in the process of converting many of its "multi-plex" theaters into "mega-plex" theaters which will have 15 or more screens, an AMC spokeswoman said.
The company is also building a 25 screen-theater in Times Square which it claims will be the largest in New York City.
AMC currently owns and operates 230 movie theaters with 1,930 screens around the world.
The company is 50.9 percent owned by management. Its chairman and chief executive officer is Stanley Durwood, whose father founded the company in the 1920s.
